articles.title: VP of Instant Replay addresses Parker Washington's non-touchdown catch
articles.summary: Following the Jaguars vs. Giants game, the VP of Instant Replay addressed Parker Washington's non-touchdown catch.
articles.body:
Early in the fourth quarter of the Jaguars vs. Giants game, it looked like Jacksonville wide receiver Parker Washington came down with a touchdown catch in the back of the end zone.

After initially bobbling the ball in tight coverage, Washington appeared to secure possession on the way to the ground while getting both feet in bounds.

However, the initial call on the field was incomplete. Liam Coen then challenged the play, but it was not overturned.

In the post-game pool report, Pat Leonard interviewed Vice President of Instant Replay Mark Butterworth, and asked about the non-touchdown catch.

"The ruling on the field was an incomplete pass," said Butterworth. "First, to overturn a call, we need clear and obvious video evidence to overturn the on-field ruling. It was determined that the receiver did not gain full control of the ball until he was out of bounds."

A follow-up question from Leonard asked for further clarification. "So, when his right foot touches the ground first, it's not determiend that he has control of the ball at that moment?" said Leonard.

To which Buttworth replied, "He needs to maintain control of the ball throughout the process of the catch."

When Washington contacted the ground, Butterworth deemed that the ball was still moving in his hands.

Instead of the touchdown making it a 20-13 game in favor of the Giants , the Jaguars had to settle for a field goal, keeping it a two-score game at 20-9. The Giants would win Sunday's matchup 23-18.

articles.title: Pierre LeBrun Reveals Stunning Dylan Larkin Trade Secret Kept Quiet for Months
articles.summary: Pierre LeBrun reveals Dylan Larkin was open to Montreal for months and explains Michael Hage's critical role in the Red Wings blockbuster trade.
articles.body:
The Dylan Larkin trade saga finally came to an end Sunday night when the Detroit Red Wings sent their former captain to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal. But according to NHL insider Pierre LeBrun , there was a major secret being kept behind the scenes for months.

And it changes the way we look at how this entire situation unfolded.

Following the trade, LeBrun revealed that Larkin had actually been willing to accept a move to Montreal for more than two months. However, the Canadiens and Larkin's representatives reportedly agreed to keep that information quiet.

"So, it turns out Dylan Larkin was actually open to a trade to Montreal for more than two months," LeBrun wrote on X, according to the post provided. "But the Canadiens wanted to keep that quiet because they felt it would add an extra layer of noise that might hamper getting a deal done. And Larkin's camp agreed."

That's a fascinating revelation considering the months of speculation surrounding Larkin's approved trade destinations.

Michael Hage Was the Key to Getting the Deal Done

According to LeBrun, Montreal had been a legitimate possibility much longer than the public realized. However, the Canadiens still had to satisfy Detroit's asking price, which reportedly included one particularly important asset.

"Montreal agreeing to include Hage was a huge must for the Red Wings," LeBrun reported. "The deal started to come together and get serious on Friday."

That detail is especially interesting considering Hage had previously emerged as a potential centerpiece in a hypothetical deal between the two organizations.

Now, we know just how important the 20-year-old University of Michigan standout was to Detroit's negotiations.

According to the NHL's official trade announcement , the Red Wings received Hage, Kirby Dach, Samuel Montembeault, two conditional first-round picks, a second-round selection, and a fourth-round pick.

Montreal received Larkin, along with Detroit's 2027 third-round and 2028 second-round selections.

LeBrun's Revelation Raises New Questions

Perhaps the most interesting aspect of LeBrun's report is how it contrasts with the information available throughout the trade saga.

Earlier this month, reports indicated Larkin's camp was unwilling to expand his approved list , even as Montreal continued expressing interest.

Now, LeBrun's latest account suggests the Canadiens had privately received Larkin's blessing long before Sunday's announcement.

That doesn't necessarily mean the earlier reporting was inaccurate. It does, however, suggest there was considerably more happening behind the scenes than the public knew.

For Detroit, the biggest takeaway may be that interim general manager Shawn Horcoff held firm on acquiring Hage rather than settling for a package without the highly regarded prospect.

And if LeBrun's timeline is accurate, a trade saga that appeared to drag on for months may have ultimately come down to one critical breakthrough on Friday.

The Canadiens finally agreed to include Michael Hage, and two days later, Dylan Larkin was on his way to Montreal.

articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six w...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls are looking to bounce back. They just went on an eight-game losing streak. Plus, they lost Caleb Wilson to a broken hand for at least six weeks.

On Sunday, they welcomed the Denver Nuggets to complete a week in which they played four games. With Nic Claxton out with an illness , Jalen Smith once again filled in at center. And it was a good thing, even though he was listed as probable due to illness himself.

He was virtually all over the floor. Smith took good shots, went for rebounds, and showed pure versatility. All of which came together in one sequence in the 2nd quarter. At the 7:53 mark, Tre Jones went for the 3-pointer, but missed. Smith grabbed the rebound and kicked it back out to Jones. Jones pumped-faked it before finding the open Buddy Hield on the wing. Hield penetrated the lane, dished it to Smith, who then slammed it down with authority.

He finished the half with 15 points and went 6-for-7 from the field. In Claxton's absence, Smith has emerged as a major catalyst at center.

Altogether, he is averaging 13.4 points and 7.9 rebounds per game while shooting 52.8% from the field. Additionally, Smith has scored in double figures in 11 games this season. His highest-scoring game came on November 11 against the San Antonio Spurs, when he finished with 23 points.

Meanwhile, Smith has bounced back from injury scares , usually stemming from aggressive play. Chicago trailed Denver 72-70 at the half.

articles.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
articles.summary: Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24, at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the hi...
articles.body:
Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday.

All the high from the Chargers' win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt.

The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA's Hayley Elwood.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame," wrote Elwood on X.

Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call.

The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half.

The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8.

The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years.

If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad.

articles.title: Five takeaways from UCLA basketball's mauling the Delaware Blue Hens
articles.summary: Five takeaways from the No. 7 UCLA Bruins 85-48 win against the Delaware Blue Hens at the Pauley Pavilion on Sunday.
articles.body:
The No. 7 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team decimated the Delaware Blue Hens with an 85-48 win at the Pauley Pavilion on Sunday.

The win concludes the Bruins five game homestand as UCLA extended their win streak to six games. The Bruins learned from their previous games and Delaware was never able to hold the lead, as UCLA continued to pile on points and blow the Blue Hens out. Here were five takeaways from their win.

The Bruins have been monsters when they run to the basket and this game was no different. In fact, this was UCLA's best game in the paint with a monstrous 52-points. The Bruins also had a good game from the field by shooting 55% and 28% from beyond the arc. That's an incredibly dangerous offense that tore through Delaware's defense and would lead to the Bruins creating a 41-point lead at one point in the game.

UCLA continued to have new players shine bright for them on a game-in and game-out basis. This time it was sophomore center Filip Jovic, who came off the bench and led the game with 17 points in his 19 minutes of play. Jovic made 7-of-8 field goal attempts, but also snagged six rebounds and had two assists.

Bruins sophomore guard Jaylen Petty was out of the lineup this game and senior center Xavier Booker returned to the starting lineup. In his return, Booker scored 10 points, grabbed four rebounds, one assist and three steals to propel his team to a monstrous lead. Booker's three steals were tied for the most of the game along with freshman forward Joe Philon III.

UCLA's defense has continued to be a focal point of the team this year with 11 steals to take complete control of the game. On top of that, the Bruins forced 11 more turnovers against the Blue Hens and scored 27 points off of the 22 turnovers. Defense opens up the offense and Delaware experienced the formula the Bruins use to win games first hand.

The Bruins had a 19-point lead heading into halftime and they didn't leave this game up to chance. UCLA silenced Delaware's offense to begin the second half and swiftly made it a blowout. It seems like the Bruins learned that they can't play with their food and defense is necessary for the entirety of the game. With the win, the Bruins are 6-0 and are in pretty good shape as they inch closer towards conference play.

San Francisco 49ers offensive lineman Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City.

McKivitz — who had played in 77 straight games entering the game — seemed to snap his lower leg while blocking during a play.

The broadcast showed his left foot seemingly twisted to the side before cutting to a timeout. When they returned, many 49ers players were visibly shaken up and taking a knee.

It is way too early to tell exactly what happened to the 30-year-old lineman. But there's no doubt that this was a very serious injury.

This is a tough loss for the 49ers, who have one of the league's best offensive lines.

But the hope right now is that McKivitz's injury isn't as bad as it looked.

There is surely more to come on his injury's severity.

articles.title: Magic fall flat, trail entire night in loss to Wizards
articles.summary: The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend road trip. With all five...
articles.body:
The Magic fell behind by as many as 25 points and never led against the Wizards on Sunday night to go 1-1 on their two-game weekend road trip.

With all five members of its starting lineup finishing in double figures, including five-time All-NBA big man Anthony Davis (22 points), Washington cruised to its third straight victory, 116-96, over Orlando inside Capital One Arena.

The Magic had a hard time keeping up with the Wizards from distance, an area of the court where Washington knocked down 56% of its 3-point shots and held Orlando to just 31% shooting on the other end.

It's the second win for Washington over Orlando this month. The Magic lost to the Wizards by nine points at home on Nov. 2, and the sides will face each other a third time in November on Saturday. The sides won't see each other again until much later in the season on April 3 for their fourth and final regular-season meeting as Southeast Division opponents.

Washington (7-11) did a solid job slowing down Magic forward Franz Wagner, who had scored 30-plus points in five of the past seven games. Wagner was limited to 16 points in the loss while teammate Jalen Suggs missed all six of his 3-point attempts to score just nine points in 22 minutes of action.

The Magic (7-9) will look to regroup at home when they host the Pistons in a big NBA Cup game on Tuesday night at Kia Center.

The Magic lacked a sense of urgency when the Wizards scored the first 11 points of the game. It took three minutes of action for Orlando to get on the board after back-to-back layups from Franz Wagner.

Washington had success pushing the ball in transition and from beyond the arc in the opening frame. The Wizards held an 11-0 advantage in fast break points and shot 6 for 11 from 3-point by the end of the first quarter.

Meanwhile, the Magic went 3 for 14 from distance in the first quarter and was outrebounded 15-7 to fall behind by 17 points, 38-21, after the opening 12 minutes of the game.

Washington entered Sunday's game shooting 31.9% from beyond the arc, which marked the third-worst 3-point percentage in the league.

But against the Magic, the Wizards could hardly miss from distance.

Orlando often failed to closeout on defense to open shooters on the perimeter and the Wizards made them pay for the disfunction. Through three quarters alone, Washington tied its season-high for 3-pointers made in a game with 18.

The Wizards finished 22 for 39 from 3-point range and had seven different players hit from distance, including guard Bilal Coulibaly who made four. Coulibaly had made a total of six 3-pointers in his first 16 games played this season.

On the other end of the floor, the Magic finished 12 for 39 from 3-point range with both reserves Nikola Vucevic and Jevon Carter both shooting 1 for 4 on the perimeter. Desmond Bane (17 points) shot 3 for 8 from 3 in 33 minutes.

One of the few bright spots for the Magic on Sunday night was the play of third-year forward Tristan da Silva.

After scoring just six points at Brooklyn on Friday night, da Silva bounced back in a major way with 18 points in 27 minutes off the bench.

Da Silva knocked down a team-high four 3-pointers when he shot 6 for 10 from the field and added three rebounds.

articles.title: SEC Rivalry Week Schedule Sets Up a Dramatic Finish With Plenty at Stake
articles.summary: BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last. Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conferenc...
articles.body:
BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference has saved some of its most anticipated matchups for last.

Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conference championship implications, postseason positioning and decades of bad blood sharing the spotlight.

Georgia has already secured its place in the SEC Championship Game. However, Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still have unfinished business.

Meanwhile, several other programs have an opportunity to close their seasons with bragging rights that last considerably longer than one Saturday.

South Carolina-Clemson's exact kickoff time and television assignment remain among the options listed by the conference.

Texas visits Texas A&M on Friday night, giving the Longhorns the first opportunity to influence the SEC Championship Game race.

A victory would improve Texas to 7-2 in conference play and place pressure on Alabama and Tennessee entering Saturday.

However, a loss would eliminate the Longhorns from contention for the conference title game.

Earlier Friday, Ole Miss hosts Mississippi State in the Egg Bowl. Florida also travels to Tallahassee for its annual meeting with Florida State.

Georgia hosts Georgia Tech in Clean, Old-Fashioned Hate, although the Bulldogs have already completed their SEC schedule.

Meanwhile, Tennessee visits Vanderbilt before Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl.

Those two games could determine which team joins Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5.

Elsewhere, Oklahoma travels to Missouri, South Carolina visits Clemson and Kentucky hosts Louisville.

The regular season has produced plenty of surprises. Nevertheless, Rivalry Week has a way of making everything that happened before it feel like an opening act.

For the SEC, the final weekend promises more than bragging rights. It will help determine the conference's championship matchup and shape its playoff representation.

articles.title: NHL Trade Grades for Blockbuster Dylan Larkin Deal Between Red Wings and Canadiens
articles.summary: Another Team USA Gold Medalist gets his wish and is traded. In this case, it's the rare move to Canada.
articles.body:
Another Team USA Gold Medalist gets his wish and is traded. In this case, it's the rare move to Canada.

Dylan Larkin is now a member of the Montreal Canadiens after being dealt in an eye-popping trade on Sunday night.

The Red Wings finally end a saga that has been hanging over their heads for a while. It's one fewer mess to clean up; Simon Edvinsson's fate remains unresolved. And then there's the greater project of selling fans on the idea that there is any sort of plan in place.

How does Larkin fit in Montreal? What do the Red Wings receive, and how does Michael Hage help them out? Let's assess the move for both the Red Wings and the Canadiens and hand out grades.

The Canadiens needed Larkin perhaps more than any other team.

A fairly strong squad that otherwise has the pieces to be a strong playoff competitor, their center group was dragging them down. Nick Suzuki is a bona fide first-line center, but the group behind him — Philip Danault, Jake Evans, and Oliver Kapanen — would have gotten clobbered in a playoff matchup against teams like Florida, Tampa Bay, or Ottawa.

For Larkin, it's a great fit as well. He is not a franchise center who can carry the load for an otherwise weak team, as he was asked to do in Detroit. He'll slip in nicely under Suzuki and provide a different profile. Larkin is speedier and more of a playmaker, and because Suzuki and Danault thrive in tough defensive minutes, Larkin will be unlocked to take on a more offensive role.

The package the Habs are parting with hurts. Michael Hage was not just their top prospect but one of the best players outside the NHL. Would it have been nice to have a middle-six center like Hage on an entry-level contract for the next few seasons? Absolutely.

But this is the type of move management can make when it builds patiently. All of Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson, Ivan Demidov, and Nick Suzuki are signed to team-friendly deals. That built-in flexibility allows the team to sacrifice the young player whose contract will be cheap for the veteran who can make an impact right away. The 30-year-old Larkin is 30 years old, and his $8.7 million contract through 2031 is itself team-friendly.

The Canadiens are still a few players away from matching the top teams in the East, but this is a massive step in the right direction for a team that is still blossoming. The Panthers and Lightning are heavily indexed in players on the wrong side of 30. This Larkin trade will make the Habs more competitive this season but may also put them over the top in the next year or two, as a potential changing of the guard is performed in the Atlantic Division.

In the context of so many things going against them, I think the Red Wings did pretty well here.

Michael Hage may not be the young NHL center they initially targeted, but he's the closest thing to one. The American has been dominant in the NCAA. As a sophomore at Michigan last season, he led the nation with 39 assists. This season, he has 26 points through 13 games. Hage is a pure play-driver who is puck-dominant; he's the guy you want in control, whether that's entering the zone or holding at the walls. With agility and intelligence, he can manoeuvre around the offensive zone to create for his team. He will probably be able to fill in as a third-line center whenever he turns pro this season, and he's not far off from second-line stature.

Kirby Dach is a 6'4" center who has a motor and blocks shots. The former third-overall pick is having an identity crisis as he hasn't developed into the first-line center originally imagined. While he shows moments of skill, his offensive processing isn't great, and he is a sluggish skater. With a fresh start, can the Red Wings help him remake his game in the form of a 35-40-point shutdown center? An unrestricted free agent in July, Dach is only 25 years old and could play a role in Detroit going forward or be traded as a fix-and-flip project at the trade deadline.

The two first-round picks that Detroit is acquiring will probably be down the board, and the value is further mitigated by the swap of mid-round picks that favors Montreal.

Given everything — the team's dire standing, Larkin's trade demand, the lack of a GM, the limited market — the return is about as good as anyone could have hoped. But now Detroit has to look in the mirror and ask some tough questions. Why did they ever think Larkin would return a top young NHL player? How did everything get so bad that their homegrown captain wanted out mid-contract? How did a substitute GM get put in place to navigate this trade?

articles.title: New Zealand’s Mitchell, Phillips frustrate India as first Test ends in draw
articles.summary: New Zealand rescued a draw on the final day, surviving 120 overs in a fighting display to finish on 239-5 at the close.
articles.body:
New Zealand fought a rearguard action to deny India as the first Test in Wellington ended in a draw on Monday, with the tourists five wickets short of converting their mammoth first-innings lead into victory.

India entered the final day needing eight dismissals to take a 1-0 lead in the series and boost their World Test Championship (WTC) hopes, but New Zealand were down to their last two specialist batters at tea.

New Zealand were ⁠239-5 in their second innings, still trailing India’s first-innings 720-9 declared by 113 runs, when the captains shook hands to end the contest.

Daryl Mitchell, who made 49 not out, and first-innings centurion Glenn Phillips (26) put on 63 for the sixth wicket on a Basin Reserve track that had been all but lifeless since the opening session and a bit of the match.

“I think we knew it was going to be a challenge to get 10 wickets on that wicket,” said India captain Shubman Gill.

“I didn’t really think having five or 10 extra overs would have helped ‌that much. We also wanted to keep our bowlers fresh with the quick turnaround.”

India will take some confidence ‌‌from their batting performance as they head to Christchurch for the second Test, starting on Friday, after six players each scored a half-century or better in a single innings.

KL Rahul (136) and Rishabh Pant (128) both hit centuries in contrasting styles, while Gill fell two runs short of the milestone.

Pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah impressed on his return to Test cricket after a year out, helping reduce New Zealand to 70-5 on the opening day, although he was used sparingly as India chased the result on Monday.

New Zealand’s match was a ⁠tale of two sixth-wicket stands, the first of 216 runs between Henry Nicholls (175 not out) ⁠and Phillips (118) that enabled the hosts to post a respectable 368 in their first knock.

The second between Phillips and Mitchell on Monday was never going to be about the tally of runs but more about how long they occupied the crease.

“Throughout the week, we’ve had some guys put their hands up,” said New Zealand captain Tom Latham.

“Not just today but also throughout ⁠that first innings. We had our backs against the wall a little bit coming into that third innings, so to be in this position now, yeah, pretty pleased.”

Phillips and Mitchell came together in the sixth over after lunch ⁠when Tom Blundell departed for 15 off the bowling of Anshul Kamboj to leave New Zealand at 176-5.

The delivery appeared to have beaten the bat before going through to ⁠wicketkeeper Pant, but Kamboj heard something, and when India reviewed, the DRS technology ⁠revealed the faintest of nicks.

In the opening session, spinner Washington Sundar made the first breakthrough by removing Devon Conway for 65, the ball popping up off the opener’s bat and pad for Pant to collect with an athletic catch.

Rachin Ravindra, the other overnight batter, followed for 37 with a ‌miscued shot off the bowling of seamer Prasidh Krishna that flew to Rahul in the slips.

India will rue a few missed chances to make further inroads into the New Zealand batting order, most notably a potential run-out that would ‌have ‌sent Mitchell back early in his innings.

The draw means New Zealand drop out of the top two in the 2025-27 WTC standings, with Australia moving up to join leaders and reigning champions South Africa. India remain fourth.

articles.title: Mati Prats señala el distinto rasero arbitral con Barcelona y Real Madrid: "Se les permite todo"
articles.standfirst: El periodista denunció en La Tribu los privilegios que, en su opinión, tienen los dos grandes del fútbol español
articles.summary: El periodista denunció en La Tribu los privilegios que, en su opinión, tienen los dos grandes del fútbol español
articles.body: La jornada liguera dejó victorias para Barcelona, Real Madrid y Atlético, pero también abrió el debate sobre las actuaciones arbitrales. Uno de los más contundentes a la hora de analizarlo fue Mati Prats, que pasó por La Tribu de Radio MARCA, en su habitual conversación con Pablo Villa, para poner el foco en el distinto trato que considera que reciben Barcelona y Real Madrid por parte de los colegiados. El periodista se detuvo especialmente en el encuentro entre el conjunto azulgrana y el Villarreal, un partido que estuvo marcado por varias acciones controvertidas y por las protestas de Hansi Flick. "No ver el penalti que le hicieron al Lamine a tres metros como estaba, que es un penalti como una catedral...", comenzó señalando. Pero su crítica fue más allá de la decisión inicial: "Es que le llaman del VAR y se tira dos minutos viendo la jugada en el monitor. Pero, oye, si es un penalti tan claro, ¿a qué cojones está esperando el árbitro con perdón para pintar el penalti?". Prats aseguró entender también el enfado del Villarreal y puso sobre la mesa una situación que, a su juicio, se repite en los partidos de Barça y Madrid. "Los árbitros permiten mucho al Madrid y al Barça", afirmó antes de enumerar algunos de los comportamientos que considera que no se sancionan con la misma severidad en otros equipos. "No es normal que Mourinho esté pegando voces todo el partido en la banda y no pase nada. No es normal las que lían Flick y su equipo en el banquillo. No es normal", insistió. Mati Prats fue todavía más contundente al referirse a las protestas de los futbolistas durante los encuentros. "Se les permite todo al Barça y al Madrid. Todo", sentenció. El periodista puso como ejemplo la actitud de Fermín López durante el partido ante el Villarreal: "Fermín fue un coñazo, con perdón, ayer dándole la vara al árbitro todo el partido". Una situación que comparó con la que, según su análisis, también protagonizan jugadores del Real Madrid: "Igual que pasa en el Madrid con Bellingham y compañía". Para Prats, el problema está en que ese comportamiento no tiene las mismas consecuencias cuando lo protagonizan futbolistas de otros equipos. "Eso en otros equipos no se permite", recalcó. El periodista también apuntó a la presión que soportan los colegiados cuando dirigen a los dos grandes del fútbol español: "Entiendo que cuando un árbitro pita a un grande, tenga un poquito más de precaución por la que le puede caer durante la semana". Sin embargo, dejó clara cuál debería ser la premisa para evitar cualquier diferencia de criterio: "Pero hay que pitar igual para todos". La conversación con Pablo Villa también abordó otra de las acciones que generaron debate durante el Barcelona-Villarreal: la jugada del córner y el criterio para revisar este tipo de situaciones. "Si saca rápido el córner, no te lo reviso. Yo eso lo siento, pero no lo compro", explicó el presentador. Su valoración fue tajante: "A mí eso me parece una chapuza. Nunca me ha quedado claro desde el Mundial esto cuándo sí, cuándo no, cuándo se pita, cuándo le avisan". Y terminó con una reflexión que resume su malestar con el criterio arbitral: "Depende de la pillería y la rapidez de los jugadores. A mí eso no me hace ninguna gracia".

articles.title: Gerwyn Price: Wayne Mardle says Welshman knows he can win World Championship again after fourth Grand Slam title
articles.summary: Is Gerwyn Price the favourite to win his second world title at Alexandra Palace after beating Gian van Veen in the Grand Slam of Darts final?; you can watch the World Darts Championship live on Sky Sports from December 11
articles.body:
'The Iceman' had not won a major televised event since 2022 and may have thought it might not happen again after losing three finals this year alone.

But with Luke Littler and Luke Humphries exiting early, Price took his chance with a brilliant 16-11 win over Gian van Veen in Wolverhampton .

Price claimed Grand Slam glory for the first time since 2021 - the same year he won his sole world title, when he was forced to celebrate behind closed doors due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

"Gezzy knows he can win it. Yes, winning the Grand Slam four times is amazing for him, but he knows he can win the Worlds," said Mardle.

"He's done it before and he's got a new-found fanbase.

"He's enjoying himself and it's incredible the way that everything's turned around for him. And, look, he's enjoying life.

Looking ahead to Ally Pally, 'Hawaii 501' said: "Those that are at the top of the tree right now, call it top six, top five, top four, they're the ones to beat. They really are.

"Luke Humphries, Luke Littler, Gezzy Price.

"Let's be honest, we know that he got beat [in the semi-finals] and didn't play great but Michael van Gerwen shone this week.

"Don't rule out a fourth world title for him. With timing and a bit of luck, anyone can win."

'Price is talking about the next one already'

Mark Webster said it does not look like Price is done after returning to the winners' circle with his eighth major title.

Price will be eyeing further televised success at the Players Championship Finals which takes place at Butlin's Minehead Resort from November 27-29.

Van Veen, Humphries and Van Gerwen will also headline, as a 64-player field compete in the final tournament before the 2027 World Darts Championship.

"He's still got tournaments to win. He's talking about the next one already," said Webster.

"He goes to Minehead and he's talking about this trend with winning this and winning the Worlds.

"He wants another World Championship, and particularly all the heartache he's had getting to finals this year, to get over the line, really important for him. It could open up some floodgates for him now to go on and win major after major."

The 2008 Lakeside world champion believes the cream will rise to the top on the grandest stage of them all.

"At the Worlds, there'll be upsets, but I think it will come to the top players," said Webster as Price aims to follow Michael Smith, Humphries and Littler - twice over the past four years - to win the Slam and then go on to win the Worlds in just over a month.

"I think the two Lukes left this event - they just got beat by the better player. There's no real concern in the way they played, so they'll be a force, along with Price, Gian, and it's good to see Michael [Van Gerwen] in glimpses, but it's going to be a brilliant three weeks at Ally Pally."

Has winning the Grand Slam done Price a huge favour?

Victory for Price means he is provisionally up to world No 3, with Littler still No 1, Van Veen at No 2, and Humphries down to No 4 - potentially shaking up the draw heading into the Worlds.

Price, who took home the £200,000 jackpot in Wolverhampton, has also overtaken Littler with the most ranking money earned this season.

Commentator Dan Dawson explained: "Price has had to battle to this title, and I think he's had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.

"But I think that's what he's had to do to become a winner again, and seeing him smile and seeing that pressure lift, just hearing him talk, I think that is an enormous sign because he's already looking ahead. What can I win next?

"We know that at Ally Pally he is up into No 3 in the world, with Humphries and Littler on the same side of the draw provisionally.

"That game there between Gian and Price, that would provisionally be the semi-final in the other half of the draw.

"So that has done him a favour if he is looking to become a world champion again."

articles.title: Predicting WWE Survivor Series WarGames 2026 Match Card Winners, Storylines to Emerge
articles.summary: WWE rolls into Daikin Park in Houston on Saturday for the 2026 Survivor Series: WarGames premium live event, featuring the culmination of the Bloodline vs. 946 rivalry in the marquee spot.
articles.body:
WWE rolls into Daikin Park in Houston on Saturday for the 2026 Survivor Series: WarGames premium live event, featuring the culmination of the Bloodline vs. 946 rivalry in the marquee spot.

What can fans expect from that blockbuster main event and the other three matches on the card?

Find out in this preview of the annual Thanksgiving weekend tradition.

Women's World Championship: Becky Lynch vs. Liv Morgan

Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan will write the latest—and potentially final—chapter of their rivalry Saturday night, with the latter's Women's World Championship on the line.

Lynch winning would be an appropriate conclusion, and it would net The Man her first world title since the spring of 2024. She has been one of the brightest spots in the women's division in the two-plus years since and has earned another run with the gold.

Unfortunately for her, there appears to be a long-term storyline in place for Morgan that should take her through WrestleMania 43, for which she will need to be champion.

She wins here, but not without considerable help.

Keep your eyes on Roxanne Perez, though, whom Lynch pointed out is being held back by the Judgment Day leader.

The match may provide another hint of dissension between The Prodigy and Morgan, especially as WWE loves to start planting WrestleMania seeds at Survivor Series.

Participants: Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Je'Von Evans, LA Knight and a mystery fifth participant (USA) vs. Rey Mysterio, Penta, Rey Fenix, Dragon Lee and a mystery fifth participant (Mexico)

There is no major animosity between the opposing teams or anything beyond pride at stake, but Saturday's 5-on-5 Traditional Survivor Series Tag Team Elimination match may steal the show based on the talent already announced.

While the fifth member of each team has yet to be revealed, there is a wealth of big names involved, many of whom have been responsible for some of the best in-ring action of the year in WWE.

One would expect Team USA to pull out the win considering the star power at play, but there is tension between the participants, including the unannounced fifth member, whom Rhodes teased has a history with Punk.

Add in the fun-filled struggle for power between Rhodes and Punk that feels very much like the foundation for a WrestleMania program, and you have plenty of reason to believe Mysterio and Co. can coexist long enough to pull off an upset win.

If there is one storyline to keep an eye on here, it is the mounting tension between Rhodes and Punk. Both have been good sports about their disagreements and have delivered some of WWE's best television as bickering co-captains. But both Superstars have egos, and eventually their shared desire to be recognized as No. 1 will rekindle a rivalry that was never really settled at SummerSlam in August.

Even with that tension, it does not feel like WWE has the nerve to book the upset and have Mexico triumph over the United States.

Participants: Jade Cargill, Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley, Lainey Reid and Michin vs. Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer

The heels, led by Cargill, have gotten the best of Flair and Co. for months, making life a living hell for the babyfaces and even sidelining them on occasion. The Queen recently returned from injury, and Bliss and Paxley are still reeling after losing the women's tag titles as a result of The Storm's interference.

Bayley's issues with Cargill and Co. stem from a single backstage beatdown, while Vaquer has no prior beef with any of her opponents, at least not on the main roster, making her involvement that much more curious.

Still, the match should be good given the talent involved, even if it is the one on the show that doesn't offer any long-term storylines to follow. Instead, this is all about wrapping things up and moving on.

With that being the case, the babyfaces go over here.

Prediction: Flair, Bliss, Paxley, Bayley and Vaquer

Expectations for The Rock at Survivor Series ⭐

Booking Moves WWE Must Make to Save SmackDown 🙏

Participants: The Bloodline (Roman Reigns, Jey Uso, Jimmy Uso, Solo Sikoa and Jacob Fatu) vs. The 946 (Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Cruz Montana, Lucien Price and Bronco Nima)

The months-long storyline writes its latest (but not final) chapter Saturday inside WarGames when The Bloodline and The 946 do battle.

In years past, it would be easy to look at this match as The Bloodline's to win. WarGames is typically the culmination of a rivalry.

Reigns and Co. have enjoyed considerable success in these contests, conquering whichever faction has been silly enough to oppose them. In most instances, this would be no different.

But this situation is different. The 946 has been one of WWE's highlights lately: a hot new faction mixing rejuvenated talent with fresh faces. Beating them here neuters a group with plenty more chaos to cause.

Considering Reigns has nothing to keep him busy between now and the Royal Rumble, and has yet to face Keys one-on-one, Saturday's encounter will be a stepping stone to a Reigns–Keys singles showdown.

Look for Keys to earn the deciding fall here, probably on one of the Usos, and set himself up for a match with The Tribal Chief.

Some will expect it at the Royal Rumble, but do not be surprised if that match takes place on the first Raw of the new year to mark the anniversary of the show's Netflix debut.

articles.title: Buy or Sell Nikita Kucherov, Quinn Hughes, Matvei Michkov and the Latest NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: The American Thanksgiving holiday weekend is approaching, and we got an early treat when the Detroit Red Wings traded Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday.
articles.body:
The American Thanksgiving holiday weekend is approaching, and we got an early treat when the Detroit Red Wings traded Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday.

However, we can be thankful that several notable players are still creating a buzz in the rumor mill.

Superstar Nikita Kucherov recently stunned the hockey world by requesting a trade after informing the Tampa Bay Lightning that he wouldn't sign a contract extension with them. Meanwhile, the Minnesota Wild continue to wonder if top defenseman Quinn Hughes will re-sign with them.

The Toronto Maple Leafs have been linked to Simon Edvinsson as the Red Wings decide whether to sign or trade the young defenseman. Promising Philadelphia Flyers winger Matvei Michkov became a hot topic for trade speculation following a report that he wanted a change of scenery.

How much stock should we put into these rumors? Follow along as we determine which ones are worth buying or selling.

Matvei Michkov Wants Out of Philadelphia

On Nov. 10, ESPN's Kevin Weekes reported that Philadelphia Flyers winger Matvei Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere." He cited sources who claimed the Flyers' poor start and turmoil within the team were factors.

Weekes noted that Michkov is set to become a restricted free agent next summer and is "a prime trade candidate moving forward."

Flyers general manager Daniel Briere quickly denied Michkov wanted out, calling the report "not correct." He also said he'd spoken with the 21-year-old winger and his agent, who denied that it came from them.

Two days later, TSN's Pierre LeBrun expressed doubt that Michkov would be traded, but suggested that "where there's smoke, there's fire," adding that teams were calling the Flyers about the young winger's availability.

By week's end, the situation seemed to be settling down. On Nov. 14, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that Briere and Flyers hockey operations president Keith Jones met with Michkov during a recent road trip to let him know that they wouldn't trade him because of his importance to the franchise.

Weekes' report warrants attention, even though Briere said both Michkov and his agent denied that it originated with them.

It's no secret Michkov was unhappy with his usage and had public spats with teammates Travis Konecny and Nick Seeler. This story may have been a shot across the front office's bow.

The Flyers want to build around Michkov and other youngsters like Porter Martone. If he gets a larger role and more playing time, this potentially explosive situation will be successfully defused.

Toronto Maple Leafs Could Be Interested in Simon Edvinsson

Since the regular season began, the Detroit Red Wings and Simon Edvinsson have been locked in a standoff. The 23-year-old defenseman is a restricted free agent whom the Red Wings hope to re-sign, but he prefers to be traded.

Edvinsson must sign an NHL contract by 5 p.m. ET on Dec. 1 to be eligible to play in the league this season. However, both sides remain in a staredown.

On Nov. 16, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that several teams were interested in acquiring and signing Edvinsson. However, none had met the Red Wings' asking price.

The following day, TSN's Chris Johnston reported that the Boston Bruins and San Jose Sharks were among the suitors. He also believed the Toronto Maple Leafs would like to get into the bidding, but they've traded their own first-round picks in the 2027 and 2028 drafts, which could hurt their chances of acquiring him.

The Fourth Period's Dave Pagnotta reported that Edvinsson seeks between $10 million and $11 million per season on his next contract. Even if the Maple Leafs had the tradeable assets to acquire him, they lack sufficient salary cap space for this season and next to sign him.

Pittsburgh Penguins Will Peddle Erik Karlsson

The Pittsburgh Penguins surprised the experts last season by reaching the playoffs. However, they now find themselves at the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings .

On Nov. 18, Josh Yohe of The Athletic reported that Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas told the media that his club's transactions going forward would be "very future-oriented" if things didn't improve. That was taken to mean that the Penguins will be sellers in this season's trade market.

Erik Karlsson could be among Dubas' best trade chips. The 36-year-old puck-moving defenseman leads the Penguins with 19 points. He's slated to become an unrestricted free agent in July and isn't expected to be re-signed. He has a full no-movement clause , but Yohe believes he'd waive it to join a Stanley Cup contender.

Earlier this month, we listed five potential landing spots for Karlsson. They included the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and his former team, the Ottawa Senators. The Penguins could retain part of his $10 million cap hit that they carry to facilitate a trade for the right return.

Karlsson may be aging, but his offense from the blue line would make him an invaluable addition to a Cup contender seeking that type of production. Teams could prefer waiting until closer to the March 1 trade deadline to build up enough cap space to acquire him.

Minnesota Wild Could Retain Quinn Hughes For the 2027 Playoffs

When the Minnesota Wild acquired Quinn Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks last December , it was assumed they would have the superstar defenseman signed to a contract extension in July 2026.

However, he has yet to sign an extension as the first anniversary of the trade approaches.

The 27-year-old is in the final season of a six-year contract worth an average annual value of $7.9 million. Wild general manager Bill Guerin gave up promising youngsters Zeev Buium, Marco Rossi,and Liam Öhgren (and a 2026 first-round pick) to Vancouver to get him.

Hughes is taking his time deciding whether to re-sign with the Wild. On Nov. 11, Guerin said he wants to keep the 2024 James Norris Memorial Trophy winner for as long as possible. However, he's giving Hughes the time and space he needs to consider his options and to focus on his game this season.

Considering what Guerin gave up to get Hughes, there was speculation about whether the Wild GM would move him if he remained without an extension by the March 1 trade deadline.

However, Guerin indicated he's willing to retain Hughes past the deadline, even at the risk of losing him to free agency in July.

The Wild are currently among this season's top teams. If they remain there by the trade deadline, they'll keep Hughes for the playoffs. A deep postseason run could convince him to stay. If they win the Stanley Cup and he decides to test the market, Guerin can still say he was worth it.

Tampa Bay Lightning Won't Trade Nikita Kucherov

On Oct. 30, the hockey world was stunned by reports that winger Nikita Kucherov had requested a trade and wouldn't sign a contract extension with the Tampa Bay Lightning. He based the decision on what he considered a lack of communication and respect from Lightning management during contract talks.

Kucherov, 33, is among the NHL's top stars. The Lightning's all-time leading scorer , he's a two-time Stanley Cup champion. He's also won the Art Ross Trophy three times and the Hart Memorial Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award twice. Kucherov is in the final season of an eight-year contract with a cap hit of $9.5 million.

Lightning general manager Julien BriseBois released a statement indicating the club had no intention of trading Kucherov. However, some pundits wondered if BriseBois might change his mind later in the season if Kucherov remained determined to move on.

The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun reported that at least "25 teams" internally discussed the possibility of acquiring Kucherov, who has a 10-team trade list. Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman believed he'd accept a trade to the Montreal Canadiens or the Toronto Maple Leafs.

Daily Faceoff's Matt Larkin suggested the Chicago Blackhawks, Dallas Stars, New York Islanders, San Jose Sharks, Seattle Kraken, Utah Mammoth, and Vegas Golden Knights as potential destinations. The Athletic's Joe Smith proposed the Minnesota Wild as a potential destination if they don't re-sign defenseman Quinn Hughes.

The Lightning appear intent on one last attempt at a Stanley Cup run with Kucherov. His decision hasn't affected his play or his relationship with his teammates and coaching staff. BriseBois could also hope that the coming months might spark a change of heart for Kucherov.

Standings and stats via NHL.com . Salary cap and contract info via PuckPedia .

articles.title: WWE Rumors on The Rock's Return & Oba Femi Backstage Heat, Trick Williams Talks Gunther 'Punishment'
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Expectations for The Rock at Survivor Series ⭐

Many are wondering whether the impending return of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson at next week's Survivor Series premium live event will lead to more appearances from The Great One, but it doesn't sound like that's the case.

Steve Carrier of Ringside News reported that "nothing has changed regarding The Rock's WrestleMania 43 situation. As far as we understand, his commitments to Fast Forever , the next installment in the Fast & Furious franchise, are still in place."

Lead actor Vin Diesel told Variety in August, "We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio."

If they stick to that schedule, Johnson likely wouldn't be able to commit enough time to building a WrestleMania match.

Still, fans will be excited to see what Johnson has in store for his appearance at the Nov. 28 PLE. He discussed his upcoming return during Saturday's episode of College GameDay on ESPN.

"I can't wait to go back and see the WWE Universe," he said. "I mean this. I'm gonna tell this live — I would not be in the position I am today had it not been for the University of Miami and the WWE Universe. So I'm coming to Houston to say thank you, and I love you."

After putting Bronson Reed through a table and leaving him with broken ribs and a lacerated kidney, Oba Femi could have landed in some hot water backstage.

However, it sounds like Femi is just fine. During a recent Q&A, Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp was directly asked whether Femi had backstage heat, and he shut down the notion.

"No, no, it's a very much a [common] situation like that is just, nothing you can do there," Sapp said (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News). "And I've not heard of any heat."

Femi appeared to have suffered a demotion when his promo on Monday Night Raw aired during a commercial break , but Sapp made it clear that he's not being punished.

Reed was forced to stay behind in Saudi Arabia after his unfortunate injuries while the rest of the WWE roster returned home. He reportedly underwent surgery and returned home last week, and his recovery timeline is unclear.

Trick Williams Addresses Supposed 'Punishment' to Gunther

WWE United States Champion Trick Williams isn't happy with his recent dark match win over Gunther being viewed as a punishment for the former World Heavyweight Champion.

Williams appeared on the Double Coverage Podcast and clapped back at those who feel that Gunther is too good to be losing to him.

"People say, 'Oh my goodness, you know, Gunther got punished,' this, blah, blah, that, by losing to Trick Williams. Gunther got his ass whooped. Point blank, period," Williams said (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News). "I mean, he's in the ring with Trick Williams, the United States Champion, Mr. Lemon Pepper Stepper himself. What'd you expect was going to happen?"

He continued: "This ain't no punishment to Gunther. The punishment to Gunther was putting him in the ring with me, knowing that he can't hang with the big dog. Let's talk about it."

After getting out his trash talk, Williams made it clear that he respects Gunther and always wanted to share the ring with him.

"Yeah, I always wanted to work with Gunther. I mean, he's legit as they come. I mean, he's physical, you know what I mean? And he knows what he's doing," he said. "The funny thing to me is you got to understand every dog has his day. Just because a dog had his day doesn't mean it's going to be his day forever."

articles.title: Tarik Skubal and the 25 Biggest Contracts in Sports History
articles.summary: With Tarik Skubal signing with the New York Mets for nine years and $450 million, it's time to put his deal in perspective with the biggest sports contracts we've ever seen.
articles.body:
With Tarik Skubal signing with the New York Mets for nine years and $450 million, it's time to put his deal in perspective with the biggest sports contracts we've ever seen.

Remarkably (spoiler alert), when you include all sports, Skubal's $450 million haul isn't quite in the top five.

Based on nothing more than total value (rather than average annual value or total length), here are the 25 biggest contracts the sports world has ever seen.

Contract terms: Five years, $313.9 million

The jury is still out on this one. Jayson Tatum just signed his monster contract in 2025, but he more than earned it.

Tatum led the Boston Celtics to a title in 2024 and is already top-10 in franchise history in points, threes and defensive rebounds. Given the Celtics' illustrious history, that's no small feat.

Tatum ruptured his Achilles after signing this contract, which could affect the way it ages. But he will go down as a Celtics legend regardless of how he performs on the remainder of this deal.

Contract terms: Nine years, $324 million

This is a monster deal for a starting pitcher who can play only about a fifth of a season, even in a healthy year. But Gerrit Cole has largely been worth the New York Yankees' investment.

In his first five years there, he had a 3.12 ERA, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times and won the award in 2023.

However, Cole missed the entire 2025 campaign after undergoing Tommy John surgery, and he went only 10-9 in 2026. He's under contract through 2028, so there's some downside risk on the back end of this deal.

The early returns on Giancarlo Stanton's big payday were strong.

Over his first three years on the deal (starting in 2015), Stanton had a .934 OPS and averaged 37.7 home runs a year. In 2017, he had 59 jacks and 132 RBI, was named the National League MVP and led the NL in WAR.

But the Miami Marlins traded Stanton to the New York Yankees after that monster campaign, and injuries may be the defining characteristic of his time there.

Over his nine years as a Yankee, Stanton has played just 84.9 games and hit 21.0 home runs per year.

22. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Los Angeles Dodgers

Contracts like this aren't as common for pitchers, since starters only take the mound every five games. And in today's game, starts are generally much shorter than they were in previous eras.

But the Los Angeles Dodgers paid a pretty penny to bring Yoshinobu Yamamoto over from Japan, and he hasn't let them down.

Yamamoto finished in the top four of Cy Young voting in both 2025 and 2026. And in his first two years in L.A., Yamamoto was 7-1 in the postseason with a 2.25 ERA, two World Series wins and one World Series MVP.

Corey Seager has struggled with availability since signing this contract in 2022, but he quickly made the deal worthwhile after his second season with the Texas Rangers.

In 2023, Seager hit .303 and had a 1.106 OPS in the postseason. By the time the Rangers were celebrating their World Series win, he was the obvious choice for World Series MVP.

Even though he's missed more than 40 games a year with Texas, his regular-season production has been solid, too. Since signing this contract, Seager has averaged 27.4 home runs and 70.8 RBI per year.

Bryce Harper entered the majors as one of the most hyped prospects in baseball history. During his seven seasons with the Washington Nationals, he had a .900 OPS, averaged 26.3 home runs per season, made six All-Star teams and won National League MVP in 2015.

That convinced the Philadelphia Phillies to break the bank on him in 2019 when he was 26. Although injuries and inconsistency have been more common in Philly than they were in Washington, the Phillies have still gotten a solid return on their investment.

In his eight seasons with the Phillies, Harper has made three All-Star teams (including one in 2026). He won NL MVP in 2021 and helped guide the Phils to the World Series in 2022, where they lost to the Houston Astros. And his .904 OPS in Philadelphia is slightly better than what he had for the Nats.

It's tough to view Max Verstappen's massive deal with Red Bull Racing as anything but an unqualified success.

Since signing it, Verstappen has won two Drivers' Championships and helped lead Red Bull Racing to two Constructors' Championships.

Beyond his dominance on the track, Verstappen has been at or near the forefront of F1's ascent to more mainstream attention during this deal.

Josh Allen has yet to lead the Buffalo Bills to a Super Bowl title. He'll ultimately be judged on whether or not he gets there.

But for about as long as Allen has been Buffalo's starting quarterback, he's been one of the league's most productive players. He has turned the Bills into a regular-season winning machine.

In the season and a half since he signed this deal, the average Allen game includes 18.7 completions on 27.6 throws, 1.5 passing touchdowns and 1.0 rushing touchdowns. And Buffalo is 21-6 in those contests.

17. Fernando Tatís Jr., San Diego Padres

After just two seasons and 143 total games, the San Diego Padres rewarded 22-year-old Fernando Tatis Jr. with a eye-popping 14-year, $340 million deal.

Given how young he was and how little he'd shown in the majors, the size of the contract was a surprise. And it was a roller coaster from the start.

In his first season on the deal in 2021, Tatis led the National League with 42 homers and finished third in MVP voting. Then, he missed all of 2022 with an injury and a suspension for PED use.

Things have leveled out in the four years since then, but an .810 OPS and 4.6 WAR per year don't scream $340-million player.

The New York Mets didn't wait until Francisco Lindor hit his 30s to sign him to this near-decade-and-a-half-long contract, but that hasn't stopped it from raising some concern.

Lindor has hit more home runs and driven in more runs since signing his deal, but his pre-contract OPS and batting average were higher. He made four All-Star teams prior to landing this contract in 2022. He has only had one since.

Although he did help the Mets get to the 2024 NLCS, his massive deal still hasn't led to a ton of postseason success.

It's way too early to judge this contract for either Manchester City or Erling Haaland. He just signed it in 2025.

But considering the fact that he was only 24 when he inked the deal, it's not hard to imagine this aging well.

In the nearly two years he's been on this contract, Manchester City has won the English Cup and the English FA Cup. And Haaland's 44 Premier League goals in that span dwarf João Pedro's 26, who's in second place.

Locking up the sport's best finisher before his 25th birthday—one who could be one of the best ever—will almost certainly look good in hindsight.

Manny Machado's traditional power numbers (like home runs and RBI) haven't dipped too much in recent years, but there's still some concerning writing on the wall here.

Over the eight seasons leading up to this contract, Machado hit .282, had an .856 OPS and averaged 31.3 homers, 90.5 RBI and 5.3 WAR per year.

Then, he signed this megadeal in 2023 at the age of 30. And his production has tailed off a bit.

In the four years since signing, Machado has a .256 batting average, a .771 OPS and averages of 29.0 homers, 95.5 RBI and 2.8 WAR per year. In 2026, the dropoff to 1.4 WAR and a career-worst .217 batting average was steep.

As Machado ages into his mid-30s, he's unlikely to suddenly start hitting like he did in his prime.

Contract terms: Nine years, $360 million

Like a lot of baseball greats in recent years, the back end of Aaron Judge's contract could be rough. He was already 30, had won an American League MVP and had a season with 62 home runs when he signed this deal in 2023.

But his injury-plagued 2026 aside, the early returns here are excellent.

Judge led the majors in wins above replacement and OPS in both 2024 and 2025. He was the back-to-back AL MVP in those seasons, too.

Although New York Yankees are ultimately judged on the number of World Series they win (Judge doesn't have one yet), it'll be hard to look back on this stretch of his career with anything but awe over his power.

The wildest transaction of Mookie Betts' career remains his trade from the Boston Red Sox. The success he's had with the Los Angeles Dodgers proves it.

Boston may have been scared to be on the hook for Betts' biggest contract, but he's helped L.A. win two more World Series since he signed this 12-year deal in 2021 (bringing his career total to four).

While he's certainly on the decline now, Betts has still made four All-Star teams during this contract and led MLB in wins above replacement in 2023.

His career Dodgers numbers are going to be dragged down by the post-prime ones, but in the first four campaigns of this deal, he hit .283, had an .899 OPS and averaged 29.0 home runs and 80.5 RBI per year.

Contract terms: Five years, $365 million

In 2018, DAZN made history by signing 28-year-old middleweight Canelo Álvarez to a massive deal worth at least $365 million that guaranteed the network 11 fights.

But neither the boxer nor the promotion would be satisfied. And just two years after the ink dried on this contract, it was over.

In their brief run together, Álvarez competed in just three of the 11 fights he was supposed to.

He sued the company in 2020 for its alleged failure to pay what he was expecting. The parties settled a few months later , and both went their separate ways.

Contract terms: Nine years, $385 million

In 2017, when Brazilian football star Neymar was just 25, he was widely regarded as one of the world's top three players alongside Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

Paris Saint-Germain brought him in to be the focal point of a team it hoped could win the Champions League, but he never took them to that peak. Within a few years, a young Kylian Mbappé overtook Neymar as the team's best player.

Ultimately, Neymar didn't even fully play out this contract for PSG. After years of injuries and disappointment, Saudi club Al Hilal paid a hefty transfer fee to take Neymar in 2023.

Contract terms: 12 years, $426.5 million

When Mike Trout signed this contract with the Los Angeles Angels in 2019, he looked like the second coming of Mickey Mantle.

In the first nine years of his MLB career, he won three American League MVP awards and led the AL in WAR five times. He hit .305, had an even 1.000 OPS and averaged 31.7 home runs per season.

Trout's contract was massive, but he looked like he'd be worth it. However, his Angels tenure ever since has mostly been defined by injuries and disappointment.

Since signing this megadeal, Trout has averaged fewer than 85 appearances per season. He's hit .265 and averaged 23.3 home runs a year.

And most importantly, he hasn't led his team to the playoffs once in that span.

Contract terms: Nine years, $450 million

The jury is obviously still out on this one. The two-time Cy Young winner could ultimately prove worth every penny of this deal, but a $50 million-per-year contract that will pay a starting pitcher through his age-38 season is undoubtedly risky.

Skubal's career-high in appearances in a season is 31. He's only appeared in eight postseason games. And he's been among the league's most dominant pitchers for only three years.

But over those three seasons, he has two Cy Young wins, a 2.42 ERA and a 43-17 record. And for a team desperate for playoff success, having a legitimate ace in the rotation is crucial. For at least the next couple of years, Skubal should be exactly that.

7. Vladimir Guerrero Jr., Toronto Blue Jays

This is a tough moment to analyze this deal. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. signed it in April 2025. And in the first year of this 14-year contract, his production fell off a cliff.

Over the first seven years of his career with the Toronto Blue Jays, Vlad Jr. averaged 3.7 WAR, 26 home runs and 84 RBI per season. He had an .861 OPS over that same stretch. But in 2026, he had just 1.1 WAR, nine home runs and 57 RBI while posting a .688 OPS.

Guerrero is only 27. It's too early to think this decline could be permanent. But he'll have to be worlds better for several seasons to live up to this contract.

Granted, Vlad had a different take when speaking with Spanish-language reporter Veronica Batista in September 2026.

"I want people to understand one thing. The money they gave me wasn't for what I'm going to do. It was for what I already did," Guerrero told Batista, per ESPN . "They didn't pay me because I'm going to hit 40 [home runs] every year. They paid me for what I already accomplished."

Contract terms: Eight years, $504.75 million

In 2020, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes signed a 10-year extension worth at least $450 million. Six years later, he tacked on another $200-plus million with a renegotiation that made him the first player in NFL history to ink a half-billion-dollar contract.

When Mahomes signed his initial deal, he was only 24 and already had one Super Bowl win and one MVP. It seemed like a relatively safe bet, even at that exorbitant number.

Six years later, Mahomes has two more Super Bowls, two more Super Bowl MVPs and another regular-season MVP under his belt. Even though he tore his ACL and LCL late in the 2025 season, the Chiefs had no reservations about making him the highest-paid player in NFL history for the second time in his career.

As long as Mahomes is upright, the Chiefs have a chance to beat anyone most years.

Contract terms: 2.5 years, $536.3 million

This one's tough to analyze through the "how well did this deal age?" lens.

Cristiano Ronaldo had spent much of his adult life as one of the best football players on the planet, but he was 37 when Al Nassr paid him this fortune to join the Saudi Pro League.

He was past his prime. Everyone knew it. But the team and the league wanted Ronaldo for the attention he'd bring.

Contract terms: Four years, $674 million

Lionel Messi was 30 years old when he signed this deal in 2017. He may not have been the most explosive version of himself, but he was still near the peak of his footballing powers and was one of the game's best creators and finishers throughout the duration of the deal.

Individually, he was always in the hunt for the Ballon d'Or. He won the sixth of his career in 2019. Over the life of the deal, he led Barcelona and La Liga in both goals and assists.

And it wasn't just empty-calorie production. During this contract, Barcelona won two La Liga titles, two Copa del Rey titles and one Supercopa de España.

Shohei Ohtani had a dreadful, injury-marred 2026 postseason. And by the end of this contract, his production will likely pale in comparison to what he's doing now.

But just three years into this monster deal, it's hard to imagine it looking like anything but a success for the Los Angeles Dodgers. After all, they won the World Series in each of his first two seasons in L.A.

In the regular season, Ohtani averaged 46.3 homers and 104.3 RBI per season while batting .290 and posting a .985 OPS as a Dodger. But his production isn't just limited to offense. He's a unique two-way spectacle.

While Ohtani didn't pitch in 2024, he had an ERA of only 2.17 across 28 starts in 2025 and 2026. He racked up 157 strikeouts while allowing only 95 hits, 32 earned runs and 35 walks.

He was named the National League MVP in both 2024 and 2025, and he finished second to Chicago Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong in 2026.

That's right. Ronaldo is in the top five twice. Just two years after Al Nassr signed him to his $536-plus million contract, it doled out another $710 million over two years in 2025.

And once again, this feels as much like a marketing contract as it does a football one.

Ronaldo was 40 when he signed it. He did help guide Al Nassr to the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26, but his teammate, João Félix, was named the league's player of the season .

Ronaldo has generated plenty of attention for his team and league, but it's hard to imagine Al Nassr will ever fully recoup what it cost to get him there .

It's hard to believe that a five-time All-Star, six-time Silver Slugger and near-perennial MVP contender was something of a journeyman before signing his massive contract, but that's sort of what Juan Soto was.

Before the New York Mets paid him the fortune you see above, he had already played for three teams, and he lasted less than two full seasons at two of those stops. He was sort of a bat for hire, and the Washington Nationals, San Diego Padres and New York Yankees were all wary of the massive deal they knew he'd eventually get.

The Mets weren't, though. They didn't just back up the Brinks truck for him in 2024. They brought a whole train into the station and signed up to pay the slugger into his 40s.

The early returns on the contract have been good, though maybe not spectacular. Soto led the National League in on-base percentage, walks and steals in 2025. He's hit 70 homers in his two years there, finished third in NL MVP voting in 2025 and made the All-Star team in 2026.

However, Soto still hasn't led the Mets to the playoffs. And his slight decline at the start of this contract makes the back half even more nerve-racking.

It's hard to see deals like Soto's without thinking about the disappointing twilights of Albert Pujols and Alex Rodriguez.

articles.title: Luke Littler: World No 1 faces nightmare route at World Championship with Luke Humphries a potential semi-final opponent
articles.summary: Luke Littler could face a nightmare draw at Alexandra Palace with a potential semi-final showdown against Luke Humphries; you can watch the World Darts Championship live on Sky Sports from December 11
articles.body:
Littler crashed out of the Grand Slam of Darts after a shock last-16 defeat to Jermaine Wattimena in Wolverhampton last week .

His exit follows quarter-final losses at the World Series of Darts Finals and the European Championship and a first-round defeat at the World Grand Prix.

Littler is now not due to play until the opening night of the World Championship on December 11, having failed to qualify for the Players Championships Finals in Minehead at the weekend.

'The Nuke' is projected to be the top seed for the 2027 PDC World Darts Championship, putting him on a potential semi-final collision course with Luke Humphries while keeping him apart from Gian van Veen and Grand Slam winner Gerwyn Price until the final.

Before that, the 19-year-old from Warrington could face a tricky third-round showdown against former semi-finalist Dave Chisnall, with two-time champion Gary Anderson a potential fourth-round opponent.

They famously met in the semi-finals of the Grand Slam in 2024, which Littler memorably won in a deciding leg thriller.

If Littler gets through that, he is likely to face three-time winner Michael van Gerwen or two-time semi-finalist, Nathan Aspinall.

Then it could be a repeat of the 2024 final against Humphries for a spot in the January 3 showpiece where Van Veen or Price may await.

Price, who took home the £200,000 jackpot in Wolverhampton, has overtaken Littler with the most ranking money earned this season and means he is provisionally up to world No 3, with Littler still No 1, Van Veen at No 2, and Humphries down to No 4 - potentially shaking up the draw heading to Alexandra Palace in December.

In the 128-player bracket at the Worlds, all players enter in the opening round.

The top 32 players on the Order of Merit are seeded and cannot meet until the third round. Assuming all higher-ranked seeds win their matches, Littler's projected opponents by round is as follows:

Round 1 - Unseeded international or ProTour qualifier (ranks 65-128)

Round 2 - Unseeded Order of Merit or ProTour qualifier (ranks 33-64)

Last 16 - Gary Anderson (World No 16) or Luke Woodhouse (World No 17)

Quarter-finals - Michael van Gerwen (World No 8) or Nathan Aspinall (World No 9)

Semi-finals - Luke Humphries (World No 4) or Jonny Clayton (World No 5)

Final - Gian van Veen (World No 2) or Gerwyn Price (World No 3)

Commentator Dan Dawson says Price's victory over Van Veen to claim his fourth Grand Slam title has "done him a favour".

He explained on Sky Sports : "Price has had to battle to win this Grand Slam more than he has in any other since his first, because we've seen him play unbelievable stuff to win Grand Slam titles.

"But I think that's what he's had to do to become a winner again, and seeing him smile and seeing that pressure lift, just hearing him talk, I think that is an enormous sign because he's already looking ahead. What can I win next?

"We know that at Ally Pally he is up into No 3 in the world, with Humphries and Littler on the same side of the draw provisionally.

"That game there between Gian and Price, that would provisionally be the semi-final in the other half of the draw.

"So that has done him a favour if he is looking to become a world champion again."

articles.title: NHL injury update: What happened to Zach Hyman as the Edmonton Oilers face fresh concerns after Hurricanes defeat
articles.summary: Discover the latest updates on Zach Hyman's injury as the Edmonton Oilers face new challenges following their defeat to the Carolina Hurricanes. Join us for insights on his condition and potential return against the St. Louis Blues.
articles.body: The Edmonton Oilers have received another concerning injury update involving Zach Hyman after the forward left their 7-4 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes during the second period. Hyman did not return to the contest, and his early departure became a major talking point following the game.He had a migraine, apparently, that affected his vision, head coach Mike Babcock said, with an unusual explanation for the winger's absence. The latest development adds to Edmonton’s injury troubles as the team tries to find some consistency on the road trip.Zach Hyman injury update raises concerns for Edmonton OilersEdmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock said Zach Hyman exited the game against the Carolina Hurricanes with vision problems due to a reported migraine. The coach did not provide a specific recovery timeline, leaving the forward's availability uncertain.Hyman recorded just 8:48 of ice time before leaving the contest. His absence came during a difficult second period for Edmonton, as Carolina scored five goals to establish control and eventually secure a 7-4 victory.Speaking after the defeat, Babcock addressed questions about Hyman's unexpected departure and explained that the winger was unable to continue playing.The coach indicated that the migraine had affected Hyman's vision, although he admitted that the exact implications and expected recovery period were unclear.Importantly, the explanation did not confirm a head injury. Neither the reported update nor Babcock's comments established that Hyman had sustained a concussion or another injury caused by contact during the game.The absence of a confirmed diagnosis means Edmonton's medical staff will need to assess the forward before determining his next steps.Why Zach Hyman’s latest absence is concerningHyman has had to deal with several interruptions this 2026-27 NHL season, but this latest setback is particularly frustrating, and the winger missed Edmonton's first six games before returning to action. He subsequently landed on injured reserve in late October because of a stiff neck, forcing him to miss another five contests.His production has also been below his previous standards. Hyman has four goals and six points in 14 games, far from the 54-goal season in 2023-24 and the 31-goal season last year.This latest migraine-related problem will have the Edmonton Oilers hoping this isn't another long absence.Will Zach Hyman play against the St. Louis Blues?Hyman's availability for Edmonton's matchup against the Blues: Babcock said he’s not sure what will happen with the Blues.There was no morning skate for the Oilers ahead of the game, so it was expected the winger’s status would be known during pregame warmups.If Hyman can’t go, Max Jones may get a shot at starting. Alternatively, Babcock could consider using 11 forwards and seven defensemen to adjust the team's structure.There was also a positive update involving Ryan Nugent-Hopkins. Babcock indicated that the veteran forward had received medical clearance but would not play against St. Louis, with a potential return targeted for Tuesday's home matchup against the Vegas Golden Knights.Nugent-Hopkins had missed four consecutive games before the update.For Edmonton, getting both Hyman and Nugent-Hopkins back would provide an important boost to the forward group. However, the immediate priority remains understanding Hyman's condition and determining when he can safely return to the lineup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Wellens predicts Championship future for Gilbert
articles.summary: Leyton Orient boss Richie Wellens believes midfielder Alex Gilbert is "a Championship player waiting to happen".
articles.body:
Leyton Orient boss Richie Wellens believes midfielder Alex Gilbert is "a Championship player waiting to happen".

Gilbert scored the final goal in Orient's 4-1 win over AFC Wimbledon on Saturday, with a curling effort from outside the penalty area.

Before joining Orient on a free transfer in early September, Gilbert had played 40 times in the Championship during three seasons at Middlesbrough, but only 11 of those were starts.

Wellens believes the 24-year-old is destined to one day make a success of himself in the second tier.

"He's our best player at making angles, taking it [on the] back foot, [his] range of passing, he can play through lines, he can zing it out wide," he told BBC Radio London .

"It's obviously topped off with something that he's capable of, a brilliant strike.

"There's no doubt, in my mind, that he's a Championship player waiting to happen."

Wellens was also pleased to see Dane Scarlett find the target with his third goal in 13 appearances since joining from Tottenham, and had praise for fellow forward Aaron Connolly.

"Aaron's a top player," Wellens added. "I picked him [during training] to do a penalty shootout, gaffer versus player, because I think he's one of the best players in the league - but I beat him!

"He's a top talent. He can be moany, he can be up and down with his press, but again he's set a goal up.

"When he buys into what you want to do, and his head's right, he's an unbelievable talent but then his personality can have a really powerful impact on his colleagues as well.

"I think he's in a really good place at the moment. Long may it continue."
