articles.summary: All-Marion County football team: Lawrence North running back Izayveon Moore named Player of Year.
articles.body:
Izayveon Moore is the Marion County Player of the Year by a vote of the county coaches.

Moore, the Lawrence North senior running back and Purdue commit, ran for 1,595 yards and 20 rushing TDs and caught 16 passes for 248 yards and two TDs to lead the Wildcats to a 9-3 record and Class 6A sectional championship.

For his career, Moore ran for 5,678 yards and 81 touchdowns – running for more than 1,000 yards in all four of his high school seasons – and caught 34 passes for 624 yards and seven TDs. The Wildcats won two sectional championships during Moore's high school career.

Warren Central, which finished 12-1 and won a Class 6A regional title, swept the other individual awards. Senior running back Keyon Thomas was named the Offensive Player of the Year, senior linebacker Sean Fox named the Defensive Player of the Year and J.T. Whitaker the Coach of the Year.

Thomas, an Iowa commit, ran for 1,867 yards and 25 TDs on the season going into Warren Central's 35-17 semistate loss to Brownsburg on Friday. Fox, a Kentucky recruit, compiled 114 tackles, including 17 ½ TFLs, 10 ½ sacks and two caused fumbles on the season.

Whitaker is 20-6 in his first two seasons at Warren Central, leading the Warriors to back-to-back regional championships for the first time since 2005 and '06.

articles.title: Celtics Star Jayson Tatum Passes Bill Russell in Historic NBA Milestone
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum made Boston Celtics history on Sunday night.With a deep three-pointer just before halftime, the 28-year-old overtook the legendary Bill Russell...
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum made Boston Celtics history on Sunday night.

With a deep three-pointer just before halftime, the 28-year-old overtook the legendary Bill Russell on the Celtics' all-time scoring list.

Tatum now sits eighth, with his bucket against the Golden State Warriors taking him to 14,523 points.

The MVP hopeful finished the night with 27 points, pushing his total to 14,528.

John Havlicek remains clear at the top of the charts, with 26,395 points.

Jayson Tatum Humble After Making Celtics History

As usual, Tatum did not take the achievement for granted.

Speaking after the Celtics' 88-87 loss to Golden State, he admitted it would have been better to break the record at home in Boston.

"That's cool. You know what, if I wasn't going to do it in Boston, I guess it would be the second-best place to do it at," Tatum said Sunday.

"That's cool. That's an honor. Obviously, what he meant to society, what he meant to the game of basketball, here in the Bay and, obviously, for this organization.

"So, obviously, any time you're mentioned with names like that, it's an honor, and you're doing something right."

Sam Jones is the next target on Tatum's list, and the power forward will be full of confidence after also registering his 400th 20-point game.

He becomes only the fifth Celtic to achieve that milestone.

Celtics Suffer Off-Night in San Francisco

Tatum scored 23 points in the first half of his historic night, including 10 in the opening five minutes of the match.

However, the rest of his team started slowly, although the Celtics only trailed by two points heading into halftime after some sloppy shooting from both sides.

His teammates combined to score just 19 points in the first half on 8-of-30 shooting from the field, with only 2-of-16 three-point attempts landing.

Head coach Joe Mazzulla responded by putting veteran point guard Mike Conley into the game, with the 39-year-old sinking two three-pointers to put the Celtics ahead.

Boston managed to stretch their lead to 11 in the third quarter before allowing the Warriors to fight back and take the lead with six minutes left in the fourth.

After a few back-and-forth trades, an overturned 3-pointer by Brandon Podziemski left the Celtics trailing 88-86 with 1:07 left on the clock.

Tatum managed to draw a foul and sink one of his free throws, but then went on to miss what would have been a go-ahead three-pointer and a jump shot to potentially win the game.

articles.title: TOISA 2026: Meet the nominees for Badminton Player of the Year (Female)
articles.summary: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand, set to host the annual
articles.body: The Times of India Sports Awards (TOISA) will return for its ninth edition on December 6, 2026, with Dehradun, Uttarakhand, set to host the annual celebration of Indian sporting excellence.The awards will recognise outstanding performances across disciplines during a year that featured two major multi-sport events - the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow and the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya - alongside world championships and other international competitions.The nominees for Badminton Player of the Year (Female) reflect the breadth of Indian badminton in 2026. Across the season, the shortlisted athletes and teams featured in major events, national and international competitions, and important milestones in their respective disciplines. The shortlist includes P.V. Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, among the contenders whose performances will be recognised at this year's awards.Meet the nominees for the TOISA 2026 Badminton Player of the Year (Female) award.P.V. SindhuAge: 31Key Achievements in 2026:- Won her maiden Japan Open Super 750 title, defeating reigning world champion Akane Yamaguchi in the final.- Won the Hylo Open Super 500 title in Germany, her second BWF World Tour crown of the season.- Finished runner-up at the French Open Super 750, losing to world No. 1 An Se-young in the final.- Reached the semi-finals of the Malaysia Open and Australian Open.- Climbed to world No. 5 in the BWF rankings, her highest position since November 2022.- Qualified for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, her first appearance at the season-ending event since 2021.P.V. Sindhu enjoyed a significant resurgence in 2026, winning two BWF World Tour titles, reaching another major final and climbing back into the world's top five after four years. She began her title-winning campaign with a landmark triumph at the Japan Open Super 750 in July, defeating then reigning world champion Akane Yamaguchi in the final to become the first Indian woman to win the tournament. She followed it up with the Hylo Open Super 500 crown in Germany in November, beating Denmark's Line Kjaersfeldt in the final. Sindhu also finished runner-up at the French Open, where she pushed world No. 1 An Se-young before going down in three games, and reached the semi-finals of the Malaysia Open and Australian Open. Her consistent performances across the season saw her climb to world No. 5 in the November 18 rankings, her highest position since November 2022. The two-time Olympic medallist also secured qualification for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, marking her return to the season-ending championships for the first time since 2021. The 2026 campaign marked a significant return to form for the former world champion, who once again established herself among the leading contenders in women's singles badminton.Unnati HoodaAge: 19Key Achievements in 2026:- Won the Polish Open title- Reached singles quarter-finals at the Asian Games- Made her BWF World Championships debut, progressing to the second round- Reached the semi-finals of the Taipei Open Super 300- Achieved a career-best world ranking of No. 18, becoming only the third Indian woman to break into the BWF Top 20Unnati Hooda enjoyed a breakthrough 2026 season, highlighted by her Polish Open title in March, where she bounced back from a game down to beat Ukraine's Polina Buhrova in the final. She made an impression at the Asian Games, stunning world No. 6 Putri Kusuma Wardani before reaching the women's singles quarter-finals, where she went down fighting against former world champion Akane Yamaguchi. Hooda also made her BWF World Championships debut, reaching the second round, and registered an impressive win over Thailand's Supanida Katethong at the Badminton Asia Championships. She further reached the semi-finals of the Taipei Open Super 300. Her consistent performances propelled her to a career-best world ranking of No. 18 in October, making her only the third Indian women's singles player, after Saina Nehwal and PV Sindhu, to break into the BWF top 20.Treesa Jolly and Gayatri GopichandAge: 23 year oldsKey Achievements in 2026:- Won bronze at the BWF World Championships, ending India's 15-year wait for a women's doubles medal- Reached the quarter-finals in both the women's team and individual doubles events at the 2026 Asian GamesTreesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand enjoyed a breakthrough 2026, highlighted by a historic bronze medal at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi, ending India's 15-year wait for a women's doubles podium finish. They stunned China's fourth seeds Jia Yifan and Zhang Shuxian in the quarter-finals before losing to eventual champions Liu Shengshu and Tan Ning in the semis. The duo carried their form into the Asian Games, reaching the women's doubles quarter-finals and upsetting Japan's world No. 3 pair Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto twice - once in the team event and again in the individual competition. They also reached the quarter-finals of the Denmark Open. articles.title: Timo Glock rediscovers his joy in Land Porsche test: "I couldn't stop grinning"
articles.summary: After two difficult DTM years with Dorr, Timo Glock was allowed to test the Land-Porsche at Hockenheim: Now the 44-year-old is enthusiastic and wants more
articles.body:
Timo Glock had a broad grin on his face after his surprise test day in the Land Porsche at the Hockenheimring on the 12th of October. "Now I definitely feel like carrying on," says the 44-year-old, who has two tough DTM years with the McLaren team Dorr Motorsport behind him and was given the chance by team principal Christian Land to try Bastian Buus' 911 GT3 R Evo.

It seems something clicked. "I don't think the sheer fun and enjoyment of driving have been as great in the past two years as they were today," Glock revealed in conversation with Motorsport-Total.com . "I couldn't stop grinning all day."

The conditions were anything but easy: in the morning the track was still damp - and fog meant the asphalt hardly dried. After a stint in the morning on wet tyres, the conditions only allowed slicks later in the afternoon. It was also cold, with temperatures between six and eleven degrees.

Porsche better than McLaren? "It speaks such a clear language"

Nevertheless, Glock is full of praise for the Porsche. "I know what it was like in the wet with the McLaren - or in cold conditions with a new tyre," he says. "Fundamentally, this is a completely different car - in a positive sense. It speaks such a clear language to you that you simply have a broad grin on your face."

"There's no need to talk about the sound; it's awesome anyway," Glock is also enthusiastic about the naturally aspirated six-cylinder engine, which makes significantly more noise than McLaren's turbo engine.

Still he is aware that the devil is in the detail with the Porsche as well. "When it comes to the final tenth, then you have to understand how you can exploit that certain something of the car," he says. "But it is relatively quick to understand. Everything does what it is supposed to do."

Glock praises consistency in 20-lap long run

Above all, the predictability of the car earns praise from Glock. "The systems are outstanding - ABS, traction control. It really is brutally good, and driving is simply fun. If you can do a 20-lap long run and you are within 1.5 to two tenths, then that is pretty cool."

Apart from that long run, Glock also completed four shorter stints and qualifying simulations, the majority of them on slicks. However, these were not the DTM spec tyres, which the teams had to return after the season finale, but Pirelli's DHG tyre.

Glock did not touch the car's set-up at all. "The car was quick last weekend, it was at the front in qualifying," he says, referring to the pole position for regular Land driver Buus at the season finale in Hockenheim.

"And because of the conditions, I said: for me, we don't need to tinker with the set-up, the car is absolutely fine. I just want to look, drive, understand, use the systems, adapt my driving style to the little details of the car, because as a driver you can have a relatively big influence on that."

Land: "You could see Timo's grin through the whole helmet"

Team principal Christian Land also speaks of a "great day" with Glock despite the difficult weather conditions. "After the first laps in mixed conditions, Timo came back to the pits, and you could see his grin through the whole helmet. He got used to the car very quickly and felt comfortable in various conditions."

The German says they will take "a lot of positives from this test day". It now remains to be seen whether it will remain just this one test or whether Glock and the Land team will work together again. The fact is that the team wants to expand its DTM involvement to a second car in 2027 - and the five-time DTM race winner is also thinking about continuing his career.
